text:
alex.k: Heads-up — we're scheduling a short maintenance window to mitigate recurring port flaps in az3. seeing intermittent NIC resets that correlate with small egress spikes. target window: Tue 02:00-03:30 UTC, 3 cohorts.

samira: Ack. What's the expected capacity hit? will this impact Dedicated pools?

alex.k: Estimated 8-12% capacity reduction in az3 during each cohort drain. Dedicated pools will be gently routed off nodes in the drained cohort; default fallback to cross-region for latency-sensitive tenants. No customer-facing downtime expected but tail latencies may increase for some live workloads.

ben_infra: Planning to rotate cohorts by rack groups (racks 12-15 / 16-19 / 20-23). Each cohort ~25 nodes. We'll cordon -> drain -> reboot NIC -> sanity checks -> uncordon.

jordan-oncall: Please add a canary cohort first (racks 12-13) and wait 30m for KPIs. I want to watch p99 and queue length before proceeding.

alex.k: Good call. Canary first. proceed only if p99_tokens < +15% and egress_error_rate < 0.5% vs baseline.

maya-sre: Quick reminder to disable autoscaler for affected pools during drain to avoid noisy scaling. Also I'll pre-warm KV cache on the target backfill racks after each cohort.

leo-net: On the network side we'll enable interface dampening and apply a conservative BGP flap suppression for the 90m window. That should prevent route thrash. Will coordinate with colo NOC.

ben_infra: Runbook steps (short):

```
# example steps
redwood infra cordon-cohort --racks=12-13
kubectl drain node/<node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
ssh node && sudo ip link set dev ethX down && sudo ethtool -r ethX && sudo ip link set dev ethX up
sleep 60 && run /opt/redwood/check-node-health.sh
kubectl uncordon node/<node>
```

jordan-oncall: Add the exact commands to the canary doc and tag me. I'll be live for canary.

alex.k: tagging @jordan-oncall in the doc. Also creating scheduled maintenance in ops calendar and sending customer comms for Dedicated customers with >1h notice SLA window.

opsbot: scheduled-maint created: id=mt-az3-2026-05-12-02, start=2026-05-12T02:00:00Z, end=2026-05-12T03:30:00Z, owner=ben_infra

samira: Cost question — if we route cross-region for latency-sensitive tenants during the cohort, what's the projected extra egress cost for the 90m? rough ballpark.

ben_infra: Rough estimate: ~$2.8k extra egress across the window if we push all affected traffic to eu-west1. We'll monitor and fallback to local reduced-throughput variants if cost gets high.

maya-sre: Also will enable temporary token-bucket limit increases for internal monitoring so telemetry is not dropped during the canary.

leo-net: Will run a preflight: `show interfaces counters` and `bgp summary` 10m before start and after each cohort. If packet drops >0.2% or BGP flaps >3 in 5m, we abort and rollback.

alex.k: Abort criteria noted. Postmortem owner: ben_infra. If canary stable after 30m we'll proceed to cohorts 2 and 3 with 20m spacing between cohorts.

jordan-oncall: I'll collect traces and attach the p99 plots to the maintenance doc in ops drive.

samira: ok. I'll prepare customer comms draft and run it by legal for Dedicated SLA wording.

ben_infra: final note — keep node drain concurrency at 4 nodes/rack to avoid saturating backfill racks. We'll throttle to maintain >85% cluster healthy nodes.

alex.k: Thanks all. I'll post final runbook and timeline in this thread 1h before start. :thumbsup:
